title: Travel, problems & emergencies
goal: Handle hotels and trains, report a problem or theft, get help in an emergency, and talk about 'if… then…'.
intro:
Things go wrong when you travel: a delayed train, no hot water, a lost passport. This unit prepares you for problems big and small, and gives you the words to shout for help if you ever need to.

The grammar is **conditionals**: real ones (**अगर** बारिश होगी, **तो** हम नहीं जाएँगे 'if it rains, we won't go') and imaginary ones (**अगर** मुझे पता **होता**, **तो** मैं **आता** 'if I'd known, I'd have come').

Do you have a room available?

grammar.title: Real conditions: अगर … तो …
grammar.body:
**अगर** 'if' starts the condition and **तो** 'then' starts the result. तो is almost always kept, even when अगर is dropped:

**अगर** ट्रेन लेट है, **तो** हम चाय पी लेंगे 'if the train is late, we'll have a tea'.

Tenses are flexible and natural:
**Condition** in present, future or subjunctive: अगर बारिश **होती है** / **होगी** / **हो**
**Result** in future or imperative: तो हम घर पर **रहेंगे** / घर पर **रहो**

The subjunctive (Unit 18) makes the condition sound less certain: अगर कोई समस्या **हो**, तो मुझे फ़ोन कीजिए 'if there should be any problem, call me'.

**When** works the same way: **जब** … **तब / तो** …: जब तुम पहुँचो, तो फ़ोन करना 'when you arrive, call'.

examples.native: अगर आपको मदद चाहिए, तो मुझे बताइए।
examples.roman: agar āpko madad chāhiye, to mujhe batāiye.
examples.en: If you need help, tell me.

examples.native: अगर ट्रेन रद्द हो गई, तो हम बस से जाएँगे।
examples.roman: agar ṭren radd ho gaī, to ham bas se jāyeṃge.
examples.en: If the train gets cancelled, we'll go by bus.

examples.native: अगर कल धूप निकले, तो हम घूमने चलेंगे।
examples.roman: agar kal dhūp nikle, to ham ghūmne chaleṃge.
examples.en: If it's sunny tomorrow, we'll go out.

examples.native: जल्दी चलो, वरना ट्रेन छूट जाएगी।
examples.roman: jaldī chalo, varnā ṭren chhūṭ jāyegī.
examples.en: Hurry up, or we'll miss the train.

examples.native: जब आप होटल पहुँचें, तो मुझे मैसेज कीजिए।
examples.roman: jab āp hoṭal pahuṃcheṃ, to mujhe maisej kījiye.
examples.en: When you reach the hotel, message me.

grammar.title: Imaginary conditions: अगर मुझे पता होता…
grammar.body:
For things that are **not** true or **didn't** happen ('if I were…', 'if I had known…'), Hindi uses the **-ता form without है** (the imperfect participle: होता, आता, जानती, करते…) in **both halves**:

अगर मेरे पास पैसे **होते**, तो मैं नई गाड़ी **ख़रीदता** 'if I had money, I'd buy a new car' / 'if I'd had money, I'd have bought…'

The same form covers present and past — context tells you which. Remember to make it agree: होता / होती / होते.

For the past, you'll also hear the fuller form with **होता**: अगर तुमने बताया **होता**, तो मैं आ **जाता** 'if you'd told me, I'd have come'.

examples.native: अगर मुझे पता होता, तो मैं ज़रूर आता।
examples.roman: agar mujhe patā hotā, to maiṃ zarūr ātā.
examples.en: If I'd known, I would definitely have come.

examples.native: अगर मैं तुम होती, तो पुलिस को फ़ोन करती।
examples.roman: agar maiṃ tum hotī, to pulis ko fon kartī.
examples.en: If I were you, I'd call the police. (woman)

examples.native: अगर हम जल्दी निकलते, तो ट्रेन नहीं छूटती।
examples.roman: agar ham jaldī nikalte, to ṭren nahīṃ chhūṭtī.
examples.en: If we had left early, we wouldn't have missed the train.

examples.native: काश मेरे पास ज़्यादा समय होता!
examples.roman: kāsh mere pās zyādā samay hotā!
examples.en: If only I had more time!

examples.native: अगर तुमने ध्यान रखा होता, तो यह नहीं होता।
examples.roman: agar tumne dhyān rakhā hotā, to yah nahīṃ hotā.
examples.en: If you had been careful, this wouldn't have happened.

dialogue.title: At the police station
dialogue.setting: Ben's wallet was stolen on a crowded train. He goes to the police station near Varanasi station to report it.

lines.speaker: Ben
lines.native: नमस्ते, मुझे शिकायत लिखवानी है। मेरा बटुआ चोरी हो गया।
lines.roman: namaste, mujhe shikāyat likhvānī hai. merā baṭuā chorī ho gayā.
lines.en: Hello, I need to report something. My wallet's been stolen.

lines.speaker: Policeman
lines.en: Sit down. When and where did it happen?

lines.speaker: Ben
lines.native: आज सुबह, ट्रेन में। डिब्बे में बहुत भीड़ थी।
lines.roman: āj subah, ṭren meṃ. ḍibbe meṃ bahut bhīṛ thī.
lines.en: This morning, on the train. The carriage was very crowded.

lines.speaker: Ben
lines.native: क़रीब तीन हज़ार रुपये, दो कार्ड और मेरा ड्राइविंग लाइसेंस।
lines.roman: qarīb tīn hazār rupaye, do kārḍ aur merā ḍrāiviṅg lāisens.
lines.en: About three thousand rupees, two cards and my driving licence.

lines.speaker: Ben
lines.native: नहीं, शुक्र है, पासपोर्ट होटल में सुरक्षित है।
lines.roman: nahīṃ, shukr hai, pāsporṭ hoṭal meṃ surakṣit hai.
lines.en: No, thank goodness, the passport is safe at the hotel.

lines.speaker: Policeman
lines.native: अच्छा है। अगर पासपोर्ट भी गुम होता, तो आपको दूतावास जाना पड़ता।
lines.roman: achchhā hai. agar pāsporṭ bhī gum hotā, to āpko dūtāvās jānā paṛtā.
lines.en: Good. If the passport had been lost too, you'd have had to go to the embassy.

lines.speaker: Ben
lines.en: Is there any chance of finding the wallet?

lines.speaker: Policeman
lines.native: कह नहीं सकते। अगर कुछ पता चलेगा, तो हम आपको फ़ोन करेंगे।
lines.roman: kah nahīṃ sakte. agar kuchh patā chalegā, to ham āpko fon kareṃge.
lines.en: Can't say. If we find out anything, we'll call you.

lines.speaker: Policeman
lines.native: और अपने कार्ड अभी ब्लॉक करवाइए, वरना कोई इस्तेमाल कर सकता है।
lines.roman: aur apne kārḍ abhī blok karvāiye, varnā koī istemāl kar saktā hai.
lines.en: And get your cards blocked now, otherwise someone could use them.

lines.speaker: Ben
lines.native: जी, ज़रूर। आपकी मदद के लिए धन्यवाद।
lines.roman: jī, zarūr. āpkī madad ke liye dhanyavād.
lines.en: Yes, of course. Thank you for your help.

culture: India's single emergency number is **112** (police 100, ambulance 108 in many states). A police report is called an **FIR** (first information report) — you'll often need one for insurance; ask for a copy. On trains, keep valuables close in crowded carriages, and chain luggage under the berth on overnight journeys. Indian Railways announcements and displays are in Hindi and English (and often a regional language): listen for **प्लेटफ़ॉर्म नंबर…** and **…घंटे देरी से चल रही है** 'is running … hours late'. People are generally quick to help in an emergency — a loud **बचाओ!** or **भैया, मदद कीजिए!** will draw a crowd.
